why.title: Why it exists
why.p1: A voice agent hears more of your life than any other software. Something that close should run on a machine you can unplug: what it hears, remembers and learns stays there, and nobody else gets a copy.
why.p2: So Domia does the whole conversation on your hardware: it listens, thinks, speaks and acts through the skills you connect. Each Domia has its own name, voice and memory, and all three are yours to shape.

what.q: How is Domia different from a cloud assistant?
what.a: Domia is a voice agent that runs on hardware you own. It holds a conversation, remembers what you told it and acts through the skills you connect. Your voice is processed at home, there is no account, and you choose its name, voice and temperament.

privacy.a: They stay on your node. Audio, transcripts and memory are processed and stored on your hardware, and there is no account to sign in to. A skill you connect reaches only the service it controls. The privacy page says what is kept and for how long.

cost.a: The software is free and open source under the Apache 2.0 license. You provide the hardware it runs on.

hardware.q: What do I need to run it?
hardware.a: A machine you own, a microphone and a speaker. A thin device covers a room and delegates the heavy work; a capable machine runs every stage itself; a hub-class machine serves several rooms. Domia adapts to your hardware.

offline.a: Yes. Listening, understanding, the model and the spoken reply all run on your network, so conversation, memory and built-in tools keep working. Skills keep working when the service they control is also local; anything that lives in the cloud, such as a streaming provider, stops until the connection returns.

rooms.q: Does it work in several rooms?
rooms.a: Yes. One hub can serve a Domia per room, each with its own name and voice, through a satellite in each room. Announcing something to every room, or opening an intercom between two, is done from the console's Broadcast page, not by voice.

internet.q: Can I reach it from outside my network?
internet.a: It is made for your local network. When you are away, connect to that network through a VPN; the console is the way in.

smartHome.a: Yes, through the skills you connect; Home Assistant and Music Assistant are the providers tested every day. A known command takes the fast path and calls the skill directly. For anything else the model gets a shortlist of fitting skills and decides whether to call one or just answer.

homeAssistant.q: Does it work without Home Assistant?
homeAssistant.a: Yes. Conversation, memory, the knowledge base and built-in tools such as timers, alarms, reminders and routines need nothing else. Home Assistant and Music Assistant add the house: lights, scenes, media and whatever else you expose to them.

skills.q: How do I add a skill?
skills.a: Built-in tools such as timers, alarms and reminders work from the first turn. Other skills connect over MCP: in the console, open the Skills section of a Domia's configuration and connect an MCP server, such as Home Assistant or Music Assistant, and its tools start working. Each skill has a policy (allow, ask first or block) that you set per identity, so you can switch any of them off.

guests.a: They just talk to it. You write the knowledge base (wifi, house rules, meal times, phone numbers, local picks) and Domia answers from it. It answers only what you wrote; there is no web search.

interrupt.a: Yes. Talk over the reply and it stops and listens. On a satellite the reply pauses instead of cutting off.

memoryLayers.title: Memory: what Domia remembers
memoryLayers.intro: Five layers, all kept on the node. All of them can reach the prompt: recent turns always, facts and knowledge when they are relevant, episodes and the user model once per session. Reflection writes facts, episodes and the user model when it is idle.

pills.inPromptSession: in the prompt, once per session

recentTurns.name: Recent turns
recentTurns.description: The last exchanges, in the prompt.
recentTurns.example: "And the kitchen too." Domia knows which light you mean.
recentTurns.hint: A rolling window of the latest exchanges from the current session. It is always in the prompt, so a follow-up resolves without repeating yourself.

facts.name: Facts
facts.description: Things you told it, in the prompt when relevant.
facts.example: "The dog is called Nala and sleeps in the kitchen."
facts.hint: Extracted after the turn by a reflection pass in the background, never by the reply itself. Recalled by relevance to what you just said.

knowledge.name: Knowledge base
knowledge.description: What you wrote for it (wifi, house rules), in the prompt when relevant.
knowledge.example: "Guest wifi is casa-guest. Bins go out on Tuesday night."
knowledge.hint: Notes you author in the console or through the API. They are searched by relevance and added to the prompt when they match the request.

episodes.name: Episodes
episodes.description: Summaries of past sessions, in the prompt once per session.
episodes.example: "Last week you planned a dinner for six and asked for a shopping list."
episodes.hint: A short summary written by reflection once a session ends. The latest ones are loaded into the prompt once per session, not searched on every turn.

userModel.name: User model
userModel.description: Who you are to it: interests, habits and how familiar you are.
userModel.example: "Prefers short answers and no small talk."
userModel.hint: A short picture of you: interests, tendencies and preferences. Reflection updates it between sessions.

memoryLayers.footer: Everything stays on the node. Nothing is persisted on a peer; context travels inside a delegated request.
memoryLayers.link: See the Memories screen in the console

noscript.heading: Phrase

outcome.confirm: Locks, alarms and sirens skip the fast path. By default Domia asks first: “{question}”
outcome.matchConfirm: Matched without the model, and it asks first by default: “{question}”

yes.label: Yes
yes.title: Handled without the model
yes.hint: Matched against the command templates your skills bring.

no.label: No
no.title: The model decides
no.hint: It sees the skills that fit the request and either calls one or answers in its own words.

consoleTour.title: The console, screen by screen
consoleTour.intro: A read-only demo of a real mesh of Domias runs online; every screen below is a capture of the real console.
consoleTour.openDemo: Open this screen in the live demo
consoleTour.caption: read-only demo of a real mesh

conversations.title: Conversations
conversations.summary: Every interaction on the mesh with its transcript, reply, audio, latency per stage and a grade.

turnList.title: Transcript and reply
turnList.body: Each row is one turn: which flow handled it, what was heard and what was answered.

stageTimings.title: Latency per stage
stageTimings.body: The bar splits each turn into speech to text, model and speech; open a row for the exact timings.

replay.title: Listen to it
replay.body: Play what was heard or what was answered; open the turn to grade it or run it again.

domias.title: Fleet
domias.summary: One card per identity with its role, latency and volume, and a page where its whole configuration is edited live.

glance.title: One card per Domia
glance.body: Name, temperament, role, latency and volume at a glance; the full configuration is edited live on its page.

openDomia.title: Open a Domia
openDomia.body: Each card opens that Domia's page, where you apply a template or edit its configuration; most edits reload live.

thinClient.title: Thin clients
thinClient.body: A thin client keeps wake word and audio local and delegates the rest; its routines are set on its own page and its satellites on the Satellites screen.

templates.title: Templates
templates.summary: System and custom templates, each a full configuration you apply to any Domia or compare with what it runs now.

systemTemplate.title: A system template
systemTemplate.body: Standalone runs the whole voice chain on one machine; inference hub, thin client and tuned variants ship beside it.

modelAndVoice.title: What a template carries
modelAndVoice.body: The chips preview model and voice; underneath sit engines, delegation and skills.

applyToNode.title: Apply to a Domia
applyToNode.body: Pick a Domia and apply; the node restarts with its new role, and later edits reload live.

memories.title: Memories
memories.summary: What each Domia remembers: facts, episodes and the user model, browsed here in their own tabs and edited on each Domia's page.

layers.title: Three layers
layers.body: Facts, episodes and what each Domia knows about you sit in their own tabs; search or narrow to one Domia just below.

facts.title: A fact
facts.body: Each fact names the Domia that learned it, when, and how confident it is.

trace.title: Trace back
trace.body: Confidence plus a link to the turn that produced it; episodes and the user model are checked the same way.

overview.title: Overview
overview.summary: The whole mesh at a glance: who is online, how fast replies start, and how much has been said.

latency.title: Perceived latency
latency.body: From the end of your sentence to the first sound of the reply, shown as the median with the slowest turns beside it.

localExecution.title: Local execution
localExecution.body: How many turns were handled by the Domia that heard them instead of being delegated to another one.

presence.title: Local mesh map
presence.body: Every discovered Domia appears with its role and whether it is online right now.

broadcast.title: Broadcast
broadcast.summary: Rooms talk to each other from the console: an announcement reaches every room or just one, and an intercom links two rooms live.

intercom.title: Intercom
intercom.body: Open a live channel between two rooms, so people talk to each other through their Domias.

composer.title: Type or record
composer.body: Type a message or record a clip in the console; each room plays it in its own Domia's voice or as the original recording.

targets.title: Every room or one
targets.body: Pick the rooms that should hear it, or select them all; delivery is confirmed room by room.

satellites.title: Satellites
satellites.summary: Every microphone and speaker in the rooms: which Domia it serves, what it can do and when it was last seen.

summary.title: At a glance
summary.body: How many satellites are connected or offline, how many of each kind, and how many can announce or open an intercom.

row.title: One satellite
row.body: Its status, the Domia it is assigned to, its capabilities and the last time it was seen; play a test sound or an announcement from the row.

chat.title: Chat
chat.summary: Text chat with any Domia, no microphone needed; every exchange is a real interaction.

identityPicker.title: Pick a Domia
identityPicker.body: Choose which identity answers; its mood and capabilities show on the right.

conversation.title: The conversation
conversation.body: Each reply shows its text, its audio and a link to its trace. In the online demo the chat is read-only.

composer.title: Message box
composer.body: Type, record or upload a recording, and choose whether the reply comes back as text or voice.

emotions.title: Emotions
emotions.summary: Mood per identity over time: eight axes, the current radar, and the events that moved them.

axes.title: Emotion trend
axes.body: Eight axes over time for the selected Domia; toggle the chips to compare them.

baseline.title: Current mood
baseline.body: The radar shows where each axis sits right now against the character's baseline.

events.title: Emotion events
events.body: Each shift is an event with its cause and how far each axis moved, written by the reflection after the turn.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.summary: Time to first audio, the latency breakdown per stage, model performance and the labeled evaluation set.

perceived.title: Perceived latency
perceived.body: Measured from the end of your sentence to the first sound of the reply; the median is what people actually hear.

onDevice.title: On-device share
onDevice.body: How many turns finished on the device that heard them instead of on a hub; model performance and the evaluation set follow below.

breakdown.title: Latency breakdown
breakdown.body: Speech to text, model and speech averaged over voice replies, with the moment the first audio starts marked on the bar.

settings.title: Settings
settings.summary: Console appearance, live refresh and the rotation of the shared mesh secret; further down, the nodes it syncs from and the local data it keeps.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.body: Light, dark, or following the system.

liveRefresh.title: Live refresh
liveRefresh.body: How often the live views ask the mesh for fresh data.

secretRotation.title: Mesh secret rotation
secretRotation.body: Rotate the shared secret node by node; during the grace window both the current and the next one are accepted.

pipeline.title: The voice pipeline: one spoken turn
pipeline.intro: Pick a real turn and press play: every bar is a stage of that turn, at the moment it really happened.
pipeline.stageLabel: Timeline of one real spoken turn across seven lanes, from your voice to the reply you hear
pipeline.headline: This turn: first sound {seconds} s after the last word.

mic.label: You speak
mic.note: captured on the device until you pause
mic.tip: The wake word and voice activity detection run on the device; your speech is captured until a pause is detected.

stt.label: It understands
stt.note: the transcript is ready right after you stop
stt.tip: With a live microphone the text builds while you are still talking. These turns were sent as recordings, so here it runs right after the last word.

routing.label: It decides
routing.note: a known command runs at once; otherwise the model takes it
routing.tip: A known command skips the model; anything else goes to it. The routing section below shows the decision with your own phrases.

llm.label: It thinks
llm.note: builds the prompt, then writes the reply
llm.tip: The prompt is assembled from the persona, the current mood, facts about you, your notes and the last turns. Words then stream out as they are generated.

skill.label: It acts
skill.note: only when the model decides to call a skill
skill.tip: The model sees a short list of the skills that fit the request. If it calls one, the node checks that skill's policy, runs the call (several at once if needed) and replies from the skill's own answer or from a second pass of the model that reads the result.

tts.label: It talks
tts.tip: As soon as a sentence is complete it is turned into speech, while the model keeps writing the next one.

hear.label: You hear it
hear.note: playback starts with the first sentence
hear.tip: Playback starts with the first sentence; the rest queue behind it without gaps.

endOfSpeech.title: end of speech detected
endOfSpeech.note: silence + a small turn model agree

checkpoints.llm: otherwise → the model, with the skills that fit

routing.skillCall: calls the skill; the model reads the result

turns.skill: The door (the model calls a skill)

after.title: After the turn
after.micReopen: The microphone re-opens: just answer, no wake word.
after.bargeIn: Talk over the reply and it stops and listens.
after.reflection: Later, when idle, it reflects in the background: it updates its mood and remembers new facts.

pipeline.note: Timings come from the pipeline trace of each captured turn, on a capable desktop machine. In the project's own benchmarks on a hub-class machine, a conversation starts speaking about {seconds} s after you stop, and a known command in {lo} to {hi} ms.
pipeline.link: See the timings of every turn in the console

legend.title: Four routes a request can take
legend.fastPath: A known command calls the skill directly, without the model.
legend.model: For anything else the model sees the skills that fit and chooses: call one, or just answer.
legend.notes: The matching entries of the knowledge base reach the model before it answers.
legend.memory: Facts you told it come back when they are relevant.

home.title: At home
home.intro: A day at home with Domia, from a chat over coffee to good night.
home.needs: What you need: one capable machine with a microphone and a speaker. Lights need Home Assistant, music needs Music Assistant, and more rooms need satellites. Conversation, memory, timers, alarms and reminders need nothing else.

hospitality.title: Hospitality
hospitality.intro: Hotel rooms, rentals, a lodge: you write what guests usually ask and each room answers by voice, only from what you wrote, with the name, voice and temperament you chose for that place. Below, a real example you can watch and hear.

venues.title: Attractions and guides
venues.intro: A character at a theme park, a guide in a park or a museum, a booth at a fair. One Domia per spot, in character, with its own voice and its own notes. Visitors just talk to it.

also.title: Also, in any place
also.identities: Several Domias can live on one machine, each with its own name, voice and memory.
also.broadcast: From the console's Broadcast page you can send an announcement to every room, or open an intercom between two.
also.move: A Domia can move to another machine with everything it knows.

notes.title: Write the notes
notes.body: In the console, add short entries: wifi, rules, opening hours, meal or show times, phone numbers, your local picks.

hub.title: Run one hub
hub.body: A hub-class machine on site does the listening, the thinking and the speaking for every spot.

rooms.title: Give each spot a Domia
rooms.body: A satellite in the room or booth and its own Domia, with a name, a voice and its own notes.

companion.happens: No command here, so the model just answers, in the character and voice you gave it. Talk over it and it stops to listen, and after a reply the microphone stays open for your next sentence.

memory.line: How do I take my coffee?
memory.happens: You said it once, or asked it to remember. Facts about you stay on your node, and you can read and delete them in the console.

lights.happens: A known command: it goes straight to Home Assistant without waiting for the model.

music.line: Play some jazz in the living room.
music.happens: Not a fixed phrase, so the model picks the Music Assistant skill and fills in what to play and where. Pause, skip and volume are known commands and skip the model.

reminder.line: Remind me to take my pills at nine.
reminder.happens: Free words and a time, so the model fills in the reminder and the built-in skill stores it. It is spoken aloud at nine. Timers and alarms are built in too, as known commands.

goodnight.happens: A routine you define in the console: lights off, music off, alarm set. Its phrase becomes a known command; it runs the steps in order and answers once.

wifi.happens: You write the wifi, the house rules and the check-out time once. Every guest gets the answer by voice, and nothing leaves the property.

readingLight.happens: With Home Assistant in the property it is a known command: the reading light turns on without waiting for the model.

mealTimes.happens: Meal times and opening hours are notes. Change one in the console and the room answers with the new time.

nearby.line: Any good places to eat nearby?
nearby.happens: It recommends the places you wrote down, in your own words. It does not search the web.

character.line: Nova, do dragons really breathe fire?
character.happens: No command here, so the model answers as the character you wrote: its name, its voice, its way of speaking. Children can talk to it like a friend, at a booth or in a queue.

showTimes.happens: Show times, opening hours and where things are come from the notes you wrote for that spot. It answers only what is there.

visitorMemory.happens: What a visitor tells it stays with that Domia, so it can greet them by name later. For public spots you can switch memory off: it stops learning about visitors, and the turn log stays on the device for a limited time, where you can erase it.

exhibit.happens: A Domia per room or per piece, with the notes you wrote about it. Visitors ask in their own words; the model answers from those notes.

wakeUp.happens: A known command, so the built-in alarm is set without the model and rings in that room. There is nothing to connect.

houseRules.line: Can we use the pool after ten?
houseRules.happens: House rules, quiet hours and check-out are notes you wrote. The room answers from them, in the tone you chose for the place.

storyTime.happens: The model tells it in character, from the notes you wrote about the spot: what it is, when it was built, what to look for.

findWay.happens: Each spot knows its own surroundings because you wrote them down for it: the nearest exit, the café, the next stop on the route.

cta.subtitle: Install it once, apply a template from the console and say the wake word.

proof.title: What changes on your own network

write.title: You can write
write.body: On your own console it changes things: apply templates, edit routines, chat with any Domia and send broadcasts. In the online demo these controls are disabled.

data.title: Your data stays there
data.body: The console keeps its copy of conversations, memories and timings on your own network, and exports it when you ask.

rerun.title: Run a turn again
rerun.body: Run a recorded turn again against another model on the same recording and compare before you change anything in production.

latency.title: Latency you can read
latency.body: Per-stage timings for every turn, plus the perceived latency: the time from the end of your sentence to the first word of the reply. The demo shows the real figures of a real home, including the slow turns.

cta.title: Explore the console
cta.subtitle: A read-only copy of a real console, with real conversations behind it.

hero.title: What this website collects, and what Domia keeps
hero.subtitle: Two different things: this website, which is a few pages on the internet, and Domia, which runs on hardware you own and sends nothing to anyone.

site.title: This website
site.intro: No accounts, no advertising and no tracking across sites. The code of this website is public, so you can check it.

form.title: The contact form
form.body: Your name, address and message are sent by email to the Domia inbox so you can get a reply. The website stores them nowhere else.

analytics.title: Page statistics
analytics.body: The site counts page views and measures loading speed with its hosting provider's analytics. It sets no advertising cookies and builds no profile of you.

language.title: Your language
language.body: When you switch language, a cookie remembers the choice. It holds nothing else.

media.title: Video and audio
media.body: The demo videos and audio clips load from the site's hosting provider only when you press play.

code.body: This website is open source. Everything on this page can be verified in its repository.

product.title: Domia, on your hardware
product.intro: The software has no account, no central server and no telemetry. What it keeps, it keeps on your node.

local.title: Where things live
local.body: Audio, transcripts, memories and settings are processed and stored on the machines you run. The project receives none of it.

retention.title: What is kept, and for how long
retention.body: By default the log of each turn stays on the node for up to 90 days and its audio for about a day. Facts it learned about you stay until you delete them.

erase.title: Reading and erasing
erase.body: In the console you can read every memory and every conversation of a Domia, delete them, or switch learning off for that identity.

skills.title: What you connect
skills.body: A skill reaches only the service it controls. If that service lives in the cloud, its own privacy terms apply to what it receives.

code.body: Domia is open source under the Apache 2.0 license. What it stores and what it sends is in the code, not only in this text.

cta.title: A question about privacy?
cta.subtitle: Write and you will get a reply.

characters.title: Make your Domia a person
characters.intro: A Domia is someone: a name, a voice, a temperament and a way of speaking. Here are five from the demo setup answering the same question. Press play and hear how different they are.

yours.title: Yours
yours.body: In the console you pick the look and the voice, set the mood on a radar and write the character in your own words.
